Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Constant dull ache in lower abdomen with associated nausea and subjective fever for 2 days; no identified trigger or exposure.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Gradual onset over the last 48–72 hours; pain and nausea persistent.
- ENT symptoms: No throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, ear pain/hearing changes, or neck pain/swelling reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: History of mild constipation one week ago (resolved). No prior similar abdominal episodes; no previous hospital care or injection therapy.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug allergy: Amoxicillin (reaction not specified).  
  • Current medication: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • No regular oral medications.
- Any relevant social context: Lives with boyfriend; non-smoker; able to attend in-person visit today.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: None reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: No respiratory complaints; breathing normal per history.
- Mental status and associated features: No light-headedness, dizziness, or syncope.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (tele-consultation).
- Presence of another person: Boyfriend lives with patient but not present on call.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression: Lower-abdominal pain with nausea and mild spotting; non-ENT presentation requiring in-person assessment to rule out urinary, gynecologic, or gastrointestinal etiologies.
  Evidence: 2-day history of suprapubic ache, increased urinary frequency, subjective fever, pink spotting, sexually active, effective but not absolute contraception.
- DDx items aligned with transcript (from reasoning system):
  1. Urinary tract infection (cystitis ± early pyelonephritis) – Fits abdominal ache, urinary frequency, feverish feeling; lacks dysuria (opposing evidence).
  2. Early pregnancy or ectopic pregnancy – Pelvic pain and spotting despite implant; requires exclusion with pregnancy test; pain not acute/severe (opposing evidence).
  3. Pelvic inflammatory disease – Lower-abdominal pain, spotting, systemic symptoms; no discharge or dyspareunia (opposing evidence).
- No ENT pathology suspected.

Plan:
- Immediate actions:
  • Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for physical examination, urine dip/culture, pregnancy test, and further abdominal/pelvic assessment.  
  • Advise patient to seek urgent care (ED/EMS) if pain worsens, develops light-headedness, fainting, severe bleeding, or any new breathing/throat symptoms.
- Patient instructions:
  • Remain accompanied until reviewed; monitor symptoms.  
  • Hydration as tolerated; simple analgesia (e.g., acetaminophen) if needed unless otherwise directed.
- Follow-up:
  • Confirm appointment time with local GP clinic today.  
  • Subsequent referral to gynecology or urology based on initial findings.  
  • Review allergy record (amoxicillin) before prescribing antibiotics.
- ENT-specific: None required at present; no airway involvement.
